001: I found a part-time job at a bookstore.
Congratulations, Laura! How many hours are you going to work a week?
Well, I'm going to work on the weekends, about twelve hours in total.
And does the schedule work for you? You won't have much free time left.
Actually, the schedule works great for me because I have my afternoons free.
I'm really glad you found something so good.
002: I'm thinking about looking for a job for Saturday mornings.
And what kind of job would you like to do?
I'd love to work at a clothing store, but I don't know if they'll hire me without experience.
Don't worry about that, a lot of stores are looking for people who are eager to learn.
You're right, I'm going to drop off my resume at a couple of stores downtown.
Well, good luck, I hope they call you soon.
003: Yesterday I had my first interview for a waiter position.
Oh, really? Tell me, how did it go?
I think pretty well, although they asked me if I could work on holidays.
And what did you tell them? That's always a tricky question.
I told them yes, because I need the money to pay for my studies.
That seems like a very sensible answer to me, I'm sure they'll call you.
004: I don't know if juggling work and university will be too much.
It's tough, but a lot of people do it. How many hours are you planning to work?
They've offered me fifteen hours a week at a café.
Fifteen hours is fine if you organize your study time well.
I hope so, although I'll have to get up pretty early some days.
I'm sure you'll get used to it in no time, you'll see.
005: I need a job that lets me study in the mornings.
Then something in the afternoons would work well for you, right?
Yes, I'm looking for something at a supermarket or a shop in the neighborhood.
You could try the supermarket that opened last month.
Good idea, I've heard they're hiring a lot of people.
Well, don't hesitate anymore and go ask tomorrow.
006: I finally got a job as a sales assistant at a shoe store.
That's great, Marta! When do you start?
I start next Monday, and I'll have a two-week trial period.
And how's the pay? If you don't mind me asking.
It's not bad for a part-time job, honestly.
I'm really happy for you, truly.
007: I'm exhausted, today I worked eight hours straight at the restaurant.
Eight hours? But wasn't it a part-time job?
Yes, but today a coworker was missing and they asked me to stay a bit longer.
I hope they pay you overtime, at least.
That's what they promised me, so I didn't mind staying.
Well, then it's not so bad, but take care of yourself.
008: I've been offered a job tutoring a kid.
And what do you have to teach him? English or math?
Mostly language arts and math, three afternoons a week.
That sounds really good, and besides, the schedule is very flexible.
Yes, and they pay me better than the café where I used to work.
Well, that seems like a great opportunity to me, you should take it.
009: I don't know whether to ask for more hours at work or spend that time studying.
It depends on what you need, do you need a lot more money?
Honestly, it would help, but I don't want my grades to drop.
Then don't ask for more hours, your education is the most important thing.
You're totally right, I'd rather finish my degree without stress.
That seems like a very mature decision on your part.
010: In the end, they didn't renew my contract at the store.
Really? Wow, I'm so sorry, Javier. And what are you thinking of doing now?
Well, I've started looking for another job, but I'm not having much luck.
Don't get discouraged, I'm sure you'll find something soon.
I hope so, because I need to keep paying my expenses.
If you need anything, you know you can count on me.
